newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries recover in London ahead of auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries recover in London ahead of auction.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London recovered after selling in Tokyo, but were wary ahead of the first leg of a quarterly refunding later on Tuesday, traders and analysts said.
The U.S. Treasury will auction $17.75 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday, followed by $12.0 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10.0 billion of 30-year notes on Thursday.
"There was a bit of a London squeeze at the long end," said a trader at a Japanese bank in London. "But it wasn't really retail buying, more traders playing games."
The U.S. 30 year long bond was at 97-14 by 1030 GMT.
It was yielding 6.7 percent, after the price fell to 97-05 in Tokyo from 97-13 at the New York close. March T-bond futures were up 5/32 in automated trade at 112-20.

"The short end performed quite well, the three-to-10 year spread tightened in by about three to four points," said David Hewitt, bond strategist at Tokyo Mitsubishi in London. "It should be a reasonably successful auction.
Traders said there had been some buying of the 10s and 30s as a hedge against the auction of three-year notes later on.
"The (three-year) yield could get to 6.01 percent," said the trader at the Japanese bank here. Three-year bonds were yielding 5.97 percent by 1030 GMT.
Analysts and traders said there were few signs that the market was cheapening up ahead of this session's auction, although the 10- and 30-year's would attract more interest.
Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi in London, said he expected to see more movement ahead of Thursday's 30-year auction
"We will need to see some concessions," he said.
Hewitt said U.S. domestic accounts were likely to be big buyers, although there would be particular interest in the level of participation from central banks.
Analysts said the market had shaken off the effects of the weekend's meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations (G7), despite initial currency jitters.
"The Treasury market has held up very well. The dollar recovered its losses," said Chester. "It should be fine until we see some intervention."
June Eurodollar futures were unchanged at 94.35.
-- Lisa Wilson, Nicholas Winning, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6137
